title: How often does live --wait look for a change?
body:
**Chose:** `--wait` stats `events.jsonl` and `state.json` every 100 ms and rebuilds the snapshot as soon as either changes, and at least once a second otherwise.
**Over:** a plain full reread once a second, as the PRD's "rereads every second" reads literally.
**Because:** with 1 s polls an event appended at 1 s can be seen only at 2 s, which makes "ends a `--wait 5` within 2 s" a race. Two stats per 100 ms cost nothing; the heavy reread stays at most once a second when nothing moved.
**Undo:** set `POLL` to `REREAD` in `src/cli/live.rs`.

title: What does a finished worker's tail show?
body:
**Chose:** a worker that is not alive reads newest-first only down to its `result` line, so its `doing` and `narration` are null when the `result` is its last line, and its `running` is always null. A `STATUS: failed` result gives `outcome.status: null`, because the field lists only `done|blocked`.
**Over:** reading a finished worker's stream to the 1 MiB budget like a live one, so it keeps showing its last tool and a heartbeat that will never clear.
**Because:** the slice says a finished worker "reads only as far as its `result` line", and a dead process has no tool still running. A heartbeat with no `tool_result` after it would otherwise show a killed worker as busy forever.
**Undo:** in `read_tail` (`src/live/workers.rs`), drop the `!alive` stop on the `result` line and the final `running = None`.

title: What does a collect do when its progress sink fails?
body:
**Chose:** a sink error during the passes is returned by `run_passes` once every pass has ended, and the second opinion turns it into `fallback owed — unreviewed: <error>`, so the file is written and a respawn reruns it. A sink error on `Started` before any reviewer spawns is unreviewed the same way; on a size-skipped collect it is `collect`'s error, which the polish driver logs as "collect failed". A collect that fails before `Started` (no HEAD) still emits `collect_done {ok: false}`.
**Over:** propagating the emit error out of `collected()` and stopping the driver, or ignoring sink errors.
**Because:** the collected file's contract is that every failure after the git reads is written into it, and a failed `events.jsonl` write must not cost the reviews' spend silently nor stop polish.
**Undo:** in `src/collect.rs`, `?` the sink calls out of `second_opinion` instead of mapping them to `unreviewed`.

title: Does a CI wait on no running check emit ci_waiting?
body:
**Chose:** `ci_waiting` is emitted only for a non-empty set of running checks. A poll whose set is empty (head lag, no checks in the grace, every pending row a stale rerun row) emits nothing and leaves the dedup alone, so `["test"]`, then a lag, then `["test"]` is one event. Rows whose job link is in the watch's rerun set are left out of `checks`, as `ci::judge` leaves them out.
**Over:** emitting `ci_waiting {checks: []}` whenever the set empties, which reads as "waiting on nothing" while the board is still waiting.
**Because:** the slice says pending reasons that are not checks are not in `checks`, and is silent on an empty set; an empty event carries no check to show.
**Undo:** drop the `!checks.is_empty()` guard before the `CiWaiting` emit in `watch_ci` (`src/closeout.rs`).

title: What shape does an excerpt take in live --json?
body:
**Chose:** `gate.excerpt` and `ci.excerpt` are arrays of `{text, hit}`, one per line in log order; `hit` is false for a context line. Null when the gate is not red or CI is not red, `[]` when red and nothing matched.
**Over:** an array of plain strings.
**Because:** the extractor marks matches apart from context so a title never comes from the line above a failure; the panel needs the same mark to highlight the failing line, and strings would drop it.
**Undo:** map `excerpt_json` in `src/live/gate.rs` to the texts alone.

title: How literally does the extractor read the generic set and the always-add rule?
body:
**Chose:** `affected by [1-9]\d* vulnerabilit` (a green govulncheck prints "affected by 0 vulnerabilities"); the exit rule also matches `make[N]: *** … Error`; the last `=== N.` header is a context line, added only when something else matched, so a green log still gives nothing; tiers are exclusive: project patterns, else structured `failures[]`, else red lines with the generic set; a line rewritten with `\r` keeps its last segment; every excerpt line is cut to 300 chars.
**Over:** `affected by \d+ vulnerabilit` as written, the tier header always added and counted as a match, and CR simply deleted.
**Because:** the literal reading puts a green tier's header and "0 vulnerabilities" into every excerpt, and a header as the first match would become a red gate's block title.
**Undo:** the patterns and the selection in `src/excerpt.rs`.

title: When is ci null, and when does it carry an excerpt?
body:
**Chose:** `ci` is null only when the run has no events and no `ci/<round>.log` (an old layout, which `live_on_an_old_layout_run_is_empty_not_an_error` pins); otherwise `{state: "none", ...}` until a CI event. `ci.excerpt` is set only while the newest CI event is `ci_red`, from the newest log.
**Over:** `{state: "none"}` on every run, or an excerpt kept once the next CI round starts.
**Because:** the old-layout test requires null, and an old round's excerpt shown beside a waiting or green state reads as a current failure.
**Undo:** the early return and the `state == "red"` guard in `ci` in `src/live/gate.rs`.

title: Extend the red-check test or name a new one for the CI log?
body:
**Chose:** a new test `ci_red_writes_the_whole_failure_log` in `tests/closeout.rs`, the same scenario as `a_red_check_gets_one_fix_round_then_green`, asserting `ci/1.log` holds both stub lines, no ESC byte, and is the only file in `ci/`.
**Over:** adding the asserts inside `a_red_check_gets_one_fix_round_then_green`, as the slice's acceptance says.
**Because:** the QA plan's Prove row runs `ci_red_writes_the_whole_failure_log` by name; inside the other test there is nothing by that name to run. Costs one more two-second end-to-end run.
**Undo:** move the asserts back and drop the test.

title: The worker hook refuses a log body heredoc it reads as gh or push
body: A `docs log add … --body-file -` with a heredoc body was refused by the worker hook as a gh/git-push call (the body text seems to trip it); write the body to a scratch file outside the repo and pass `--body-file <path>`.

title: What shape does a file's sidecars take in live --json?
body:
**Chose:** a file's `sidecars` is an array of root-relative path strings (`["cp-1/home.aria.txt"]`), with no size, mtime or etag of its own.
**Over:** an array of objects shaped like a file row (`{path, bytes, mtime, etag}`).
**Because:** the PRD names the field but not its shape; a sidecar is a text dump the panel opens beside its screenshot, and a path is all it needs to fetch it. Objects can be added later as a new field without a schema bump.
**Undo:** in `row` (`src/live/evidence.rs`), map each sidecar `File` to an object instead of its `path`.

title: What does the evidence listing do where the slice is silent?
body:
**Chose:** `root` is always `"evidence"`, even when the dir is missing; a `cp-N` of this run with no dir is not listed; depth counts path components below the root, file name included (`cp-1/a/b/f.png` is 4); a dir past the depth is not walked, so what it holds is neither listed nor in `skipped`; once `--evidence-limit` is spent, later checkpoints with files are left out, not listed empty; a `.aria.txt` with no row to attach to is a `text` row captioned from the name before `.aria.txt`; a symlinked `cp-N` dir itself counts in `skipped`.
**Over:** `root: null` without a dir, empty rows for checkpoints that saved nothing, or checkpoints listed with `files: []` after the cut.
**Because:** the slice is silent on each; these keep every printed path under one fixed relative root and keep the cut a plain "newest N files" read.
**Undo:** `evidence` and `walk` in `src/live/evidence.rs`.

title: Extend the dirty-landing test or name a new one for the park reason?
body:
**Chose:** a new end-to-end test `a_park_with_no_question_carries_its_reason` in `tests/commits.rs`, the same dirty-landing scenario as `a_dirty_path_in_the_main_tree_parks_the_landing_and_keeps_the_owners_edit`, asserting while parked that the one `run_waiting` names `src/slice-01.txt` and that `live --json` has one `park` entry titled with that reason, then letting the run finish.
**Over:** adding the asserts inside the existing dirty-landing test, as the slice's acceptance says.
**Because:** the QA plan's Prove row runs `a_park_with_no_question_carries_its_reason` by name, as with AD-8. Costs one more ~4 s end-to-end run.
**Undo:** move the asserts into the existing test and drop the new one.

title: What do now and attention say where the slice is silent?
body:
**Chose:** `now` is null when the run has no events (as `ci` is on an old layout). `owner`'s `since` is the oldest open entry's opening event; `driver`'s is the newest event; `worker`'s the oldest live worker's `spawned_at`; `ci`'s the newest CI event. A `park` entry needs the newest of `run_waiting`, `run_parked`, `run_started`, `run_resumed` to be a `run_waiting` with no blocks and no asks, so a budget park after an old landing park shows no stale entry. `warn` entries have `id` `warn-<seq>`, `openedAt` their event's `ts`, `body`/`answer` null and `reason.source` `driver` (the slice's "driver otherwise"), and stay after the run ends.
**Over:** a `now` object on a run with no events, `since` from the newest event for every state, a park entry from any old empty `run_waiting`.
**Because:** the slice and PRD leave these unsaid; `live_on_an_old_layout_run_is_empty_not_an_error` pins `now` null.
**Undo:** `waiting`, `bare_park` and `warnings` in `src/live/now.rs`.

title: How wide does the redactor read the token shapes?
body:
**Chose:** the redactor reads the token list a little wider where the slice is silent: `gh[pousr]_` (every GitHub token prefix, not only `ghp_`), `ASIA` beside `AKIA`, `Bearer` and `X-API-Key:` in any case, a JSON key ending in a listed name (`"access_token"`, `"api-key"`), an env value quoted or cut at `& , ;` so a query string keeps its next pair, and the 41+ char rule on any `/`-led segment, not only inside a URL. A JWT is replaced whole; every other shape keeps the name or prefix that told it apart. Strings are cut (excerpt lines to 300 chars, narration to 160) before the redactor sees them, so a token cut across that edge can leave a partial value unredacted.
**Over:** the list read literally (`ghp_` only, case-sensitive headers, exact JSON keys) and a URL parser in front of the path rule.
**Because:** each extra is the same secret under another name, and redacting a harmless value costs a line of noise while a missed one leaks; the cut belongs to the sections that read the logs, and the slice puts the redactor at serialization.
**Undo:** trim `RULES` in `src/live/redact.rs`.

title: Are strings redacted before or after they are cut to width?
body:
**Chose:** every string a section cuts to a width (excerpt lines and failure messages at 300, the gate tail, a worker's narration, label and `BLOCK:` line at 160) has its token shapes redacted first, then is cut; the final pass over the snapshot still runs. A red gate's block title, which comes from the excerpt, is redacted too.
**Over:** AD-13's "strings are cut before the redactor sees them", which left `{"password": "correc` or half a JWT in the output whenever a secret sat across the cut.
**Because:** the security pass and the second opinion found it independently; a rule that needs a closing quote or a full length cannot match a cut string.
**Undo:** drop the `tokens(...)` calls inside the `cut(...)` calls in `src/excerpt.rs`, `src/live/gate.rs` and `src/live/workers.rs`.

title: When does a CI log count as the current red's?
body:
**Chose:** `ci.excerpt`, and a CI block's `reason`, use the newest `ci/<round>.log` only when its mtime is at or after the timestamp of the newest `ci_red` (up to the block's event); otherwise the excerpt is null and a block's source is `driver`.
**Over:** the newest log on disk whenever the state is red, which showed an earlier round's failure for a red that ended in a rerun, a head-mismatch block or the fix-round cap, none of which write a log.
**Because:** `on_red` writes the log only on the path that starts a fix, after it emits `ci_red`, and the event carries no round that names the file. Comparing times needs no new event field.
**Undo:** `current_ci_log` in `src/live/gate.rs`; call `newest_round` in its place.

title: What does live say while CI checks have not registered yet?
body:
**Chose:** kept AD-4: no `ci_waiting` while the running set is empty. So for the grace window after a new head (up to 5 polls), during a head lag, and after a flaky rerun, `now.waitingOn` reads `nothing` and `ci.state` keeps the previous `red` or `none`.
**Over:** emitting `ci_waiting {checks: []}` when the set empties, so the panel reads "waiting for checks to register"; or making `waitingOn` `ci` whenever the phase is closeout and no CI verdict followed the newest head.
**Because:** the second opinion raised it in three passes. Either remedy changes what an event or a state means, which AD-4 settled, so the owner picks. Parked as an idea with both remedies.
**Undo:** nothing changed.

title: AD-5 kept
AD-9 kept
AD-16 changed
body: now.waitingOn reads ci whenever the run is in closeout and no CI verdict (ci_green, ci_red) follows the newest head, including the grace window, head lag and a rerun. Read-side only in live; no new event, ci_waiting keeps its AD-4 meaning.
